what: The places Janela forecasts, records and decides. ONE definition: the archive extractor, the daily feed, the workability tables, the alpha audit and the page all read this file and nothing else (a site defined twice WILL diverge). A site is a point; the forecast is read on the model's own grid around it (`box` = nodes either side of the nearest node, so a later choice of the best sea node needs no re-fetch). Field sites sit on nodes of the pinned WAVEWATCH III hindcast (corpus/ww3-points) so that climate and forecast speak about the same water. Terminal sites are the terminal's position; the forecast there is the nearest OPEN-SEA model node, which is the approach, never the berth — a berth value needs the nearshore transfer, and until it exists a berth rule is REFUSED, not guessed.
